label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Kavya’s recent post about founders hiring within a cohort is about DabbaDost and me. Kavya runs SitterNest, a babysitter-booking app; DabbaDost does home-tiffin subscriptions. I’m being tagged in the comments, so I’d rather respond once, plainly, than let guesses become the story. This isn’t a fight, and I’m not trying to win a comments section. I respect her too much to turn this into a public back-and-forth.

@Kavya, first: I’m sorry. I knew from day one where both candidates worked. I should have called you before making the offers, not WhatsApped you after the second offer was accepted. That was my mistake. Whatever the hiring process was, a friend deserved that call.

I also don’t want my respect for Kavya to get lost here. Before Foundry91 Cohort 4’s demo day in March 2026, she sat with me until 1 a.m. in the Koramangala office, helping fix our Razorpay webhook mess. She didn’t have to. I haven’t forgotten it, and one bad piece of judgement from me doesn’t cancel everything she has done for me.

Some details, though, need correcting:

• Nobody from DabbaDost DM’d or approached either engineer. We posted a backend developer opening on our LinkedIn page and Instahyre on 14 September, open to anyone. The first person applied on 19 September. The second came through his referral two weeks later.

• The offers were 22% over each person’s then-current CTC, not 40%. Both joined us on 3 November.

• We did not promise ESOPs we don’t have. Our pool is small, but it is real, documented, and on paper since January.

I’m putting these dates and numbers out because “40%” and “DMing your team” are already being repeated as fact. I won’t name the two people involved. They applied for jobs; they didn’t sign up for a public discussion.

The bigger issue is real. Foundry91 has 11 startups in our batch, and we hire from the same small talent pool across HSR and Koramangala. Without some basic courtesy, this will keep happening.

Good people should be free to choose where they work. This rule is about communication between founders, not restricting anyone’s career or blocking a move.

My suggested cohort rule: if you’re interviewing someone from another batch company, give that founder a heads-up before making an offer. Not permission, not a veto; just a timely, respectful call. I’ll follow this from now on, and I wish I had followed it here.

Kavya, coffee or a call is open this week, whenever you’re okay with it. I’d rather have one uncomfortable conversation and repair a friendship than perform a disagreement on LinkedIn.
